I'm guessing that the running work like physical therapy for you knee helping it grow stronger and compensate for the weakness from injury. But at this point you may have over trained on particular muscle set that could be causing you pain as it pulls reputedly on your injured knee. Can you explain what you mean by this? Are you collapsing? Are you stopping from pain, or exhaustion?

what time do you run? could be that you may be running on empty and its your muscles running low on sugar that make you feel tired.

If you feel its your cardio holding you back, try going for a longer-ish bike ride (or stationary) or elliptical and see how you feel at that same effort level but try to go longer.

In my personal opinion, you may actually be overtraining. Not in any individual run or day, but there may not be enough rest between that max distance and the sprints. Which leads to another question: what are "sprints"? are you actually doing speed intervals around a track? I would not recommend them at your current mileage and pace. Or are you doing "strides" as in just a few 50-100 yard strides to work on your form and/or stretch out your legs; in which case, two thumbs up.
